A lots of books on English Grammar are available (a)/ in the market but (b)/ this one is the best. (c)/No Error (d)
questions.s: ‘A lots of’ का प्रयोग नहीं होगा बल्कि इसके बदले 'A lot of’ या 'Lots of', जो idiomatic है का प्रयोग होगा।

questions.q: While you are in Agra, (a) / you must not miss (b) / seeing the TajMahal, (c) / because it is a worth seeing monument. (d)/ no error (e)
o: because it is a worth seeing monument.
questions.s: Use "worth seeing monument" as "a monument worth seeing".

questions.q: The school was (very co-operation) when we made a documentary film there.
questions.s:
We need an adjective to describe the noun school.
The correct adjective form is co-operative.

questions.q: You must start your work without some farther delay.
questions.s:
(b) Explanation:- yhan meaning dena hai ' bina koi bhi aur delay ke' isliye ' any further delay' ka use hoga.

any - koi bhi

further - in addition to something.

questions.q: While you are in Agra, / you must not miss / seeing the TajMahal,/ because it is a worth seeing monument.
o: because it is a worth seeing monument
questions.s:
Explanation:- Use monument worth seeing in place of worth seeing monument. Kyunki ‘worth + V1 + ing’ se jab adjective banate hain to ing wala structure humesha worth ke baad hi lagana hota hai yeh structure aapko yaad hi karna hi.

Eg:- It is a movie worth watching.

It is a place worth visiting.

questions.q: The movie is (a) / more exciting (b) / than the book. (c) / No error (d)
questions.s: There is no error. 'More exciting' is correct for comparative degree. Answer: (d). Sentence mein koi galti nahi, 'more exciting' comparative degree ke liye sahi hai. Jawab: (d).

questions.q: Ramesh is smarter/ enough to get/ selected for this/ post, without any recommendations.
questions.s: Explanation:- Use smart in place of smarter. Kyunki yahan Ramesh ka kisi aur se comparison nahi karna hai isliye comparative degree use nahi hogi. Yahan meaning dena hai Ramesh enough smart hai.

questions.q: Unless it is accepted to both the parties, an / arbitrator would be of no / use to settle this dispute.
o: Unless it is accepted to both the parties, an
questions.s:
Explanation:- Use acceptable in place of accepted.

accepted- Jise 'accept' kar liya gaya ho.

acceptable- Jise 'accept' kiya jaa sake.

Agar 'it is accepted' ka use karenge toh veh passive structure ho jayega aur aage 'by+doer' jaise kuchh nahi likha isliye meaning ke according aur structure ke according 'it is accepted' galat ho jayega 'it is acceptable' se meaining and grammar dono theek rahenge.

questions.q: What is the / price of this / fancy dress pink? (SSC CHSL Tier-01 21/03/23)
questions.s: Adjective order is incorrect. Quality/opinion ('fancy') typically precedes color ('pink').

questions.q: That was the most worst movie I've ever seen, but this one is the best.
o: That was the most worst
movie I've ever seen,
but this one is the best.
questions.s:
In the original sentence, "most worst" contains two superlative degrees used together, which violates the rule. The correct form is simply "worst," which is already a superlative degree. So, the correct option is: (a) That was the most worst

So, the corrected sentence would be: "That was the worst movie I've ever seen, but this one is the best."

questions.q: He spends good deal of money on clothing.
questions.s:
(a) Explanation:- 'a lot of' ki tarah 'a good deal of' phrase bhi quantity dikhane ke liye use kiya jata hai.

Baki saare options yhan grammatically sahi nhi hain.

questions.s: Explanation:- Use most prolific in place of prolific. Kyunki jab do adjective 'and' conjuction se jode jaate hain toh dono same degree me likhe jaate hai.

In the original sentence, "most fastest" contains two superlative degrees used together, which violates the rule. The correct form is simply "fastest," which is already a superlative degree. So, The correct option is: (c) most fastest runner in the team.

So, the corrected sentence would be: "He is faster than his brother, but she is the fastest runner in the team."

questions.q:
The money arrived when I (little) expected it.

[Phase-X (12TH LEVEL) 02/08/2022]
o: The money arrived when I least expected it.
The money arrived when I less expected it.
The money arrived when I expected it.
The money arrived when I little expected it.
questions.s: "Least" is the superlative form of "little" and is used to express the lowest degree of expectation in this sentence.

questions.q:
In the following question, one part of the sentence may have an error. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option.

These tips and tricks (A)/ once mastered, (B)/ will help you reach your search results (C)/ more faster than anyone else. (D)
questions.s:
Part D has an error.

The double comparative 'more faster' is grammatically incorrect. The correct usage is 'faster'.

Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.

The correct sentence is: These tips and tricks once mastered, will help you reach your search results faster than anyone else.

[СРО 13/03/2019 S1]
questions.s: The comparative form of "good" is "better.”

questions.q: He is (a) / very much tired (b) / after the race. (c) / No error (d)
questions.s: The error is in part (b). 'Much' is redundant; correct form is 'very tired.' Answer: (b). 'Much' extra hai, sahi form hai 'very tired.' Jawab: (b).

questions.q: The Hindu is (1)/ most popular, than any other (2)/ newspaper in India.(3)/ No Error (4)
questions.s:
When comparing one thing with all others, we must use the superlative degree with a definite article. Also, comparison takes than, but superlative sentences normally use “the most… of/in”.
Correct Sentence: The Hindu is the most popular newspaper in India.
